hints: Look at the reagents for each reaction and ask yourself what type of alcohol reaction this is, elimination, esterification or substitution?
Remember that hot $Al_2O_3$ dehydrates an alcohol to an alkene, so reaction 1 must split out $H_2O$.
Check the other two for $H_2O$ as well, an alcohol plus a carboxylic acid gives an ester plus water, and an alcohol plus $HBr$ gives a bromoalkane plus water.
walkthrough:
**Reaction 1 - Dehydration over hot alumina**

Hot $Al_2O_3$ acts as a dehydrating catalyst. It removes $H$ and $OH$ from adjacent carbons to form a C=C double bond.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Reaction 2 - Esterification with ethanoic acid**

A warm alcohol plus a carboxylic acid with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ catalyst forms an ester. This is a condensation reaction, so water is always split out.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Reaction 3 - Nucleophilic substitution with HBr**

Warming an alcohol with $HBr$ replaces the $OH$ group with $Br$ to make 1-bromopropane. The $OH$ leaves with $H$ from the acid to make water.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Combine the conclusions**

All three reactions produce water as one product. Reaction 1 gives propene plus water, reaction 2 gives propyl ethanoate plus water, and reaction 3 gives 1-bromopropane plus water. So 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct. All three statements are true. Dehydration, esterification and substitution of an alcohol with HBr all release $H_2O$ as shown in the equations above.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. It is tempting if you forget reaction 3, but $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + HBr$ clearly gives $H_2O$ alongside the bromoalkane.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3. It misses reaction 1, but dehydration over hot $Al_2O_3$ is defined by the loss of water to form propene.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. It misses the other two. Students sometimes think only elimination makes water, but both ester condensation and $OH$ to $Br$ substitution also make water.
